page: The Vultr vhp-8c-16gb-amd is a virtual cloud instance situated in the High Performance family, utilizing x86_64 AMD EPYC processors running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 8 shared vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores using symmetric multithreading, alongside 16 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Cache architecture provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and FMA, although AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. Local storage is directly integrated, consisting of a 350 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by one public IPv4 address. The server operates without discrete hardware acceleration, featuring zero GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread CPU performance in stress-ng evaluations, placing within the top 25 percent of assessed hardware profiles, while multi-core stress testing settles into the mid-tier. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 1160.0 and a multi-core score of 5735.0, with solid performance in software compilation (7876.0) and ray tracing (10325.0), but lower performance in text processing tasks. Memory throughput reached 84.3 GB/sec in large-block reads and 63.29 GB/sec in write operations. In operational throughput tests, the configuration handled 13.03 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered 7.47 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

Hardware resource distribution pairs moderate compute capacity with high-speed local NVMe storage, making it cost-efficient for storage-sensitive and multi-threaded workloads that do not demand dedicated CPU cores. However, the shared core allocation model introduces potential latency variability under peak multi-tenant loads, and the 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation limits the feasibility of large in-memory datasets. The instance is best suited for CI/CD compilation pipelines, web application hosting, caching nodes, and relational or document database instances that leverage fast local NVMe read and write speeds.
description: Vultr vhp-8c-16gb-amd is a compute-focused instance within the High Performance product line, powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system provides 8 shared vCPUs derived from 4 physical execution cores, paired with 16 GB of RAM, a 16 MB L3 cache, and a bundled 350 GB NVMe SSD for high-throughput local storage. It does not include dedicated graphics acceleration. Benchmark metrics highlight strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng tests, alongside consistent mid-tier execution in multi-threaded workflows, software compilation, and Redis memory transactions at 13.03 million operations per second. With a compact 2.0 GB per core ratio, this configuration offers solid resource density for multi-threaded processes that prioritize local disk speed over vast memory capacities. It is well-matched for build servers, multi-tier web hosting, caching layers, and database workloads requiring swift NVMe access.
